title: SMTO-GWT-0033 — The list of computers for this request isn't valid
summary: SMTO checks which computers a request should run on before starting. The list it received didn't add up, for example no computer, more than 16, one listed twice, or a main computer that isn't in the list. Nothing was run.

headings.title: SMTO-GWT-0033 — The list of computers for this request isn't valid

html:
SMTO-GWT-0033 — The list of computers for this request isn't valid

GUID: 9b3030a6-191c-4f98-85c2-ff84e90fbd43
Slug: gateway-selection-invalid
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • SMTO checks which computers a request should run on before starting. The list it received didn't add up, for example no computer, more than 16, one listed twice, or a main computer that isn't in the list. Nothing was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Below the message box, select Show composer controls if they are hidden, then select the Target button. In Execution target, select at least one computer and no more than 16. SMTO needs between 1 and 16 different computers to run a request on.
  2. Check that one chosen computer shows ★ (primary). If none does, select Make primary next to the computer that should lead the work. The primary computer must be one of the computers you picked.
  3. Select Refresh targets, re-check your choices, then send your message again. Refreshing clears out computers that were removed or renamed since you last picked them, and the request was refused before anything ran.

What success looks like

  • The Target button shows your chosen computer (or Multiple gateways with the right count), and the request starts running.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't move an existing or scheduled Task to a different computer to get around this; start a new request instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway selection validation rejected the request: an unsupported schema_version, an empty or over-16 gateway_ids list, duplicate IDs, a primary_gateway_id outside the list, a gateway_id that disagrees with the primary, or a second supplied selection that conflicts with the first.

What this means

  • Gateway selection validation rejected its version or shape, conflicting supplied selections, invalid member count, duplicates, a primary outside the set, or a target without a usable context. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway selection validation rejected its version or shape, conflicting supplied selections, invalid member count, duplicates, a primary outside the set, or a target without a usable context.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selection version, one-to-sixteen distinct IDs, primary membership and consistency with separately supplied gateway_id.

How to fix it

  • Send one GatewaySelection {schema_version: 1, gateway_ids: 1–16 distinct IDs, primary_gateway_id in that list}, and make any top-level or context gateway_id equal the primary. For the HTTP connection test endpoint, send only a string gateway_node. Messages come from gateways/selection.py (gateways.selection.*).
  • Correct the selection shape and choose one to sixteen distinct available Gateways, with a primary in that set. A connection test accepts only its supported Gateway field.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The validated selection resolves every intended member and preserves the chosen primary.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
